data.why: The repo bundles curated, biologically-annotated GenBank/FASTA example sets specifically chosen to exercise the viewer's frameshift, intron and alignment-rendering paths; these are far more realistic than anything synthetic, small, and already the ones the README tells users to try first.

goals: load a multi-record GenBank genome and inspect its gene/CDS/regulatory annotations at base and amino-acid zoom levels
align a small set of related phage or viral genomes and read the resulting conservation heatmap to see where they diverge
find and interpret a programmed ribosomal frameshift (T7 gene 10A/10B) by zooming into the codon shift in the alignment
search a loaded sequence for a motif using IUPAC codes or fuzzy identity matching and promote a hit to a new annotation
import/export annotations (GFF3/BED/GenBank/FASTA) to round-trip a curated feature set
compare a reference genome against named variants (e.g. SARS-CoV-2 Alpha/Delta/Omicron) using a pre-aligned FASTA to spot point mutations and deletions

review.summary: The tree follows the README's workflow (load, explore down to bases and codons, search and annotate, compare aligned variants, export), and the screens I sampled support the nodes, with one exception: t17 cites a screen taken after Compare was already on. It needs fixing before filing: it blames the app for a test-file collision that hid the T7 alignment, which is the README's headline example, and it leaves out remote alignment, annotation import and project reload.
